evals.prompt: Can you design a landing page for Tallyo? It's an AI bookkeeping app for freelancers and solo consultants: it auto-categorizes expenses, tracks invoices, and estimates quarterly taxes. Plans are Free, Pro ($12/mo) and Business ($29/mo). I want it to feel trustworthy but not boring-bank. Just give me a single HTML file.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained, responsive HTML landing page whose visual direction is grounded in specific references found on land-book and specialist galleries (pricing/hero/social proof), with a written design direction and an Inspired-by list.
assertions: Browsed land-book.com plus at least one specialist gallery relevant to the brief (pricingpages.design, supahero.io or socialproofexamples.com), per the process log
Opened at least two live reference websites (not just gallery thumbnails)
A written design direction names a north-star reference with its URL and gives concrete tokens (specific font names, hex colors, and sizes)
index.html is a single self-contained file that renders a complete page (desktop screenshot shows a finished layout, not broken or blank)
Pricing section shows exactly the three plans Free, Pro $12/mo and Business $29/mo
Page is responsive: contains CSS media queries and the mobile screenshot shows a single-column layout without horizontal overflow
No lorem ipsum or generic placeholder copy for product messaging
Testimonials, customer logos or usage metrics are either absent or clearly marked as placeholders, not presented as real
Final message includes an Inspired-by list with reference URLs and what was taken from each

evals.prompt: I need a welcome email for new users of Streakly, my habit-tracking app. It should welcome them, push them to create their first habit, and mention the 3 core features (smart reminders, streak stats, friend challenges). Give me production-ready email HTML.
evals.expected_output: Production-ready, table-based, inline-styled email HTML (~600px) whose design is grounded in specific reallygoodemails references, with a design direction and an Inspired-by list.
assertions: Browsed reallygoodemails.com category or search pages relevant to the brief (e.g. welcome, onboarding, app), per the process log
Studied at least two specific reference emails (detail page, screenshot or HTML source)
A written design direction names specific reference emails with URLs and gives concrete tokens (fonts, hex colors, widths)
Email HTML uses table-based layout with inline styles and a max content width of about 600px (no flexbox/grid for layout)
Email includes a prominent bulletproof-style CTA to create the first habit
Email mentions all three features: smart reminders, streak stats, friend challenges
No lorem ipsum; copy is specific to Streakly
Final message includes an Inspired-by list with reference URLs and what was taken from each

evals.prompt: Our open-source CLI Driftwood (Postgres schema migrations, written in Rust) needs a new homepage hero and top navbar. The current one looks like a 2015 Bootstrap template. The nav needs Docs, GitHub, Changelog and Pricing (we have a hosted cloud tier). Give me the HTML/CSS for just the navbar + hero, responsive, with a proper mobile menu.
evals.expected_output: Responsive navbar + hero HTML/CSS for a Rust Postgres-migrations CLI, grounded in supahero and navbar.gallery references, with a mobile menu, design direction and Inspired-by list.
assertions: Browsed supahero.io (search-index.json or site) and navbar.gallery (a relevant /style/ or /type/ page), per the process log
Compared at least 8 candidates visually, via a contact sheet or grid screenshots
Opened at least two live reference sites and extracted real tokens (fonts, sizes, colors) from them
A written design direction names a north-star reference with its URL and gives concrete tokens (font names, hex colors, sizes)
Output is only a navbar and a hero (no extra page sections), with nav links Docs, GitHub, Changelog and Pricing
Responsive with a working mobile menu: media queries plus a toggle button that exposes the links (aria-expanded or equivalent), and the mobile screenshot shows a collapsed nav
No lorem ipsum; copy is specific to Driftwood (Postgres migrations, Rust CLI)
Social proof such as GitHub star counts, download numbers or company logos is absent or clearly marked as placeholder, not presented as real
Final message includes an Inspired-by list with reference URLs and what was taken from each
